The bias of $W$ under $\mu$ at $\theta$ is $\int_S W \, d\mu - \theta$, the expected value of $W$ under $\mu$ minus $\theta$.

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a measurable space, $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator, $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ a family of probability measures on $S$ and $\tau : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ a target function. If $W$ is unbiased for $\tau$ under the family $(P_\theta)$, then $\int_S W \, dP_\theta = \tau(\theta)$ for every $\theta \in \Theta$.

The extended frequentist risk of $\delta$ at $\theta \in \Theta$ is the Lebesgue integral $\int_S \ell(\theta, \delta(x)) \, dP_\theta(x)$, taken in $[0, \infty]$.

Then the frequentist risk $R(\theta, \delta)$ of $\delta$ at $\theta$ is nonnegative for every $\theta \in \Theta$.

nodes.title: A finite second moment makes the squared error integrable

nodes.summary: Let $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ be a family of probability measures on $S$ and $\tau : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ a target function. If an estimator $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ is unbiased for $\tau$, then $W$ is $P_\theta$-integrable for every $\theta \in \Theta$.
nodes.title: Unbiased estimators are integrable

nodes.summary: Let $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ be a family of probability measures on $S$, $\tau : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ a target function, and $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator that is $P_\theta$-integrable for every $\theta \in \Theta$. Then $W$ is unbiased for $\tau$ if and only if its family bias $\int_S W \, dP_\theta - \tau(\theta)$ is zero for every $\theta \in \Theta$.
nodes.title: An estimator is unbiased exactly when its bias vanishes

nodes.summary: Let $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ be a family of probability measures on a measurable space $S$ and $\tau : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ a target function. An estimator $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ is unbiased for $\tau$ if for every $\theta \in \Theta$ the function $W$ is $P_\theta$-integrable and $\int_S W \, dP_\theta = \tau(\theta)$.
nodes.title: Unbiased estimator

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $S$, $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$. If the squared error $x \mapsto (W(x) - \theta)^2$ is almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to $\mu$ but not $\mu$-integrable, then the extended mean squared error $\int_S (W(x) - \theta)^2 \, d\mu(x) \in [0, \infty]$ of $W$ at $\theta$ equals $\infty$.
nodes.title: Extended mean squared error of a measurable non-integrable squared error is infinite

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $S$, let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ be an estimator and let $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ be a target value. The extended mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$ is the (lower) Lebesgue integral $\int_S (W(x) - \theta)^2 \, d\mu(x)$ of the nonnegative squared error, computed in $[0, \infty]$. It is defined for every $W$, with no integrability hypothesis.
nodes.title: Extended mean squared error

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $S$, let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, and suppose the squared error $x \mapsto (W(x) - \theta)^2$ is $\mu$-integrable. Then the mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$ equals $\int_S (W(x) - \theta)^2 \, d\mu(x)$.
nodes.title: Mean squared error as an integral

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $S$, let $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, and let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ be square-integrable with respect to $\mu$, that is, $W \in L^2(\mu)$. Then the mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$ equals $\operatorname{Var}_\mu(W) + b^2$, where $b = \int_S W \, d\mu - \theta$ is the bias of $W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$.
nodes.title: Bias–variance decomposition of the mean squared error

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $S$, let $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, and let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ be square-integrable with respect to $\mu$, that is, $W \in L^2(\mu)$. Then the mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$ equals $\operatorname{Var}_\mu(W) + \left(\int_S W \, d\mu - \theta\right)^2$.
nodes.title: Mean squared error as variance plus squared mean deviation

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $S$, let $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, and let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ be square-integrable with respect to $\mu$ (that is, $W \in L^2(\mu)$) and satisfy $\int_S W \, d\mu = \theta$. Then the mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$ equals $\operatorname{Var}_\mu(W)$.
nodes.title: Mean squared error of an unbiased estimator

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $S$, let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ be an estimator and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ a target value, and suppose the squared error $x \mapsto (W(x) - \theta)^2$ is $\mu$-integrable. The mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$ is the real number $\int_S (W(x) - \theta)^2 \, d\mu(x)$.
